intervention_label: Tumor HRD genomic-instability score + somatic BRCA1/2 (FDA companion diagnostic on archival FFPE)
expected_benefit: Resolves the single highest-value decision point. A genomic-instability score >=42 (Myriad MyChoice) or a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation qualifies HRD-positive maintenance: olaparib + bevacizumab per PAOLA-1 (HRD-positive PFS HR 0.33) and single-agent olaparib per SOLO1 if somatic BRCA is mutated (PFS HR 0.30). Germline BRCA is already wild-type, so this one FFPE order covers the somatic and genomic-scar gap germline testing cannot.
key_risks: 2-4 week turnaround on archival FFPE; no fresh biopsy required
a negative HRD score and wild-type somatic BRCA forecloses the HRD-positive PARP options (ranks 4-5); niraparib and bevacizumab remain available because neither gates on the score
preference_alignment: Aligns with every stated preference: non-toxic, runs on archival tissue with no new procedure (matches her caution against additional invasive procedures and her bleeding/VTE history).
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 ties first-line maintenance selection to HRD / somatic-BRCA status; the assay is the precondition the guideline's own biomarker conditions assume.
rationale_summary: All five personas and the patient herself named the pending tumor HRD / somatic-BRCA result as the rank-1 move. The deep platinum response, R0 resection, and ctDNA clearance to Not Detected are consistent with HR-deficient biology but are not diagnostic of it. The somatic BRCA call and the genomic-instability score come from the same tumor NGS panel, so a single archival-FFPE order resolves both pending biomarkers. The result decides whether the HRD-positive PARP options (ranks 4-5) are reachable; niraparib (rank 2) and bevacizumab (rank 3) do not wait on it.
open_questions: Which companion diagnostic the treating institution uses (Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42 vs FoundationOne genomic LOH) and whether the chosen cutoff matches the PAOLA-1 / PRIMA eligibility threshold
MSI / MMR and a broad somatic panel can run on the same block to screen for dMMR (checkpoint-inhibitor eligibility) and non-BRCA HR-pathway genes (RAD51C/D, PALB2, BRIP1)
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty. Resolves HRD / somatic-BRCA status and decides whether the HRD-positive PARP options (ranks 4-5) are reachable.
toxicity_burden: Low (none - diagnostic NGS on archival FFPE)
overall: Non-toxic archival-tissue assay that gates the HRD-positive PARP options; order it before committing the maintenance strategy.

expected_benefit: PRIMA ITT PFS HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.76); mPFS 13.8 vs 8.2 mo across all-comers, deepening to HR 0.43 (0.31-0.59) in the HRD-positive subgroup. The all-comers benefit does not wait on the pending HRD score.
key_risks: grade 3+ anemia 31% and thrombocytopenia 28.7% on the fixed 300 mg start (cumulative G3+ thrombocytopenia 39.7% at 3.5 years)
engages her severe-myelosuppression / febrile-neutropenia veto; the weight-and-platelet individualized starting dose lowers but does not erase the cytopenia rates
preference_alignment: Oral once-daily: matches 'oral preferred'. In open tension with the severe-myelosuppression veto - the one ranked option that touches a stated veto, surfaced rather than hidden. The individualized starting dose is the prerequisite mitigation, not a footnote.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 category 2A first-line maintenance for all-comers after a platinum response; the warrant is PRIMA itself (low-RoB phase 3), not the consensus tier.
rationale_summary: The one PARP option active across the all-comers ITT, so it does not strictly gate on the pending HRD score the way the olaparib-based rows do. The critic ranks it first on RoB grounds; concensusite ranks it first on guideline fit; risktaker and advocate carry it for her with the individualized starting dose named up front. The conservative dissents on confidence rather than the drug, flagging that the cytopenia profile sits directly on her myelosuppression veto and must travel with the weight-and-platelet starting dose. Magnitude sharpens once the genomic-instability score returns, but the floor is real now.
open_questions: Whether the individualized starting dose holds the cytopenia rates tolerable across a multi-year maintenance window in a 70-79 patient at the older end of the PRIMA population
Mature ITT overall-survival data are weaker than the SOLO1 OS readout
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate across all-comers (PRIMA ITT PFS HR 0.62); high in the HRD-positive subset (HR 0.43). Does not wait on the pending score.
toxicity_burden: High (anemia 31%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%; cumulative G3+ thrombocytopenia 39.7% at 3.5 yr)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cytopenia-driven dose interruptions can erode maintenance dose intensity; the myelosuppression that engages her veto is itself the limiter

overall: The PARP option that does not wait on the HRD score; all-comers benefit is real but the cytopenia profile sits on her myelosuppression veto and requires the individualized starting dose.

expected_benefit: GOG-218 PFS HR 0.717 (0.625-0.824), mPFS 14.1 vs 10.3 mo from the maintenance arm; ICON7 PFS HR 0.81 with its largest survival gain in the high-risk subgroup (stage IV or stage III >1cm residual) she matched before R0 resection. PFS-only; no ITT OS benefit in either trial.
key_risks: bleeding and thrombotic events on an anti-VEGF agent given her high-VTE history and prior IVC filter - a risk already accepted in her current regimen rather than a new one
grade 2+ hypertension ~22.9% (GOG-218), the dominant and well-managed toxicity
preference_alignment: Clears both toxicity vetoes outright (no myelosuppression, no neuropathy). Partial tension with 'oral / low-infusion preferred': IV q3w, but the infusion burden she already carries. In tension with the bleeding/VTE modality caution, though that risk is built into her current plan.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 category 2A 1L maintenance in her exact indication; the backbone onto which olaparib is layered in the HRD-positive PAOLA-1 strategy.
rationale_summary: Continuing the bevacizumab she already tolerates is the lowest-regret guideline-aligned move while the HRD assay is out, and it targets the VEGF / angiogenesis axis directly rather than gating on the pending score. Conservative, critic, concensusite, and advocate all endorse it as the interim hold; the advocate and concensusite note both vetoes stay clear. The risktaker dissents that parking on the lowest-magnitude axis underspends a curative-intent window for a patient whose biology reads HR-deficient. The bleeding/VTE caution and the prior IVC filter stay on the active monitoring list. No ITT OS benefit is the honest ceiling.
open_questions: Whether to hold bevacizumab as monotherapy maintenance or position it as the backbone for an olaparib add-on once the HRD score returns
Duration of the maintenance window relative to her ongoing on-study regimen
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate for PFS (GOG-218 HR 0.717; ICON7 HR 0.81); OS gain confined to the high-risk subgroup she matched pre-resection. No ITT OS benefit.
toxicity_burden: Low (hypertension ~22.9% G2+; bleeding/thrombotic events on a VTE-risk patient; no marrow or neuropathic signal)

counter_productive_moa.description: Anti-angiogenic wound-healing impairment and the bleeding/VTE vector matter given her IVC-filter history, but the axis is already part of her tolerated regimen

overall: Lowest-regret guideline-aligned interim that clears both vetoes and holds the VEGF axis steady; modest PFS-only magnitude with no ITT OS gain.

expected_benefit: PAOLA-1 ITT PFS HR 0.59 (0.49-0.72); the benefit concentrates in the HRD-positive subgroup - PFS HR 0.33 (0.25-0.45), mPFS 37.2 vs 17.7 mo, 5-year OS 66% vs 48%. She is already on bevacizumab, so this adds olaparib rather than starting a new regimen.
key_risks: compounded bleeding / VTE risk: a PARP inhibitor stacked onto ongoing anti-VEGF therapy in a patient with high-VTE history and a prior IVC filter
grade 3-4 anemia 17% (vs <1% on bevacizumab alone) and hypertension 19%; the anemia brushes her myelosuppression veto from a second direction
preference_alignment: Efficacy-leaning fit (0.7) if HRD-positive - the largest effect on the board. But it spends her bleeding-risk budget and adds a second anemia source, so it is conditional on a concrete bleeding/VTE and CBC monitoring plan being on the table.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 category 1 for HRD-positive disease (ESMO concurs); the endorsement is reserved for HRD-positive tumors, so it is conditional on the pending assay.
rationale_summary: Conditional on HRD-positive confirmation. The conservative issued a rank-1 veto on toxicity grounds - a PARP stacked onto ongoing bevacizumab in a high-VTE patient with a prior IVC filter, with PAOLA-1 grade 3-4 anemia 17% brushing her marrow veto from a second direction. That veto was explicitly contingent: it stands 'unless and until the HRD score returns positive and a concrete bleeding/VTE and CBC monitoring plan is on the table.' In the HRD-positive branch with that monitoring plan documented, the veto lifts and the row stands at considered_with_caveats; the conservative and advocate dissents on the compounded bleeding/anemia load persist because they do not depend on the biomarker. Risktaker (rank 1), critic (rank 3), and concensusite (rank 2, their conditional front-runner) carry it for the HRD-positive subgroup's HR 0.33 - the biggest available magnitude. Foreclosed if HRD is negative, where the add-on loses its category-1 footing and the choice collapses back toward bevacizumab alone.
open_questions: Whether a concrete bleeding/VTE and CBC monitoring plan satisfies the conservative's veto-lift condition in this specific patient
The ITT OS was not significant; the 5-year OS gain rests on the pre-specified HRD-positive subgroup
scenario_label: If HRD-positive (Myriad MyChoice GIS >=42, FoundationOne genomic LOH-high, or a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation)
likelihood_of_effect: High in the HRD-positive subset (PAOLA-1 HR 0.33; 5-yr OS 66% vs 48%); the largest effect on the board. Foreclosed if HRD-negative.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (hypertension 19%, anemia 17% vs <1% on bev alone, lymphopenia 7%; compounded bleeding/VTE on a prior-IVC-filter patient)

counter_productive_moa.description: Anti-angiogenic plus PARP stack raises the bleeding/VTE vector that her IVC-filter history already flags; the conservative dissent rested on this mechanism

overall: The largest-magnitude option when HRD reads positive - but only with a documented bleeding/VTE and CBC monitoring plan, because it stacks PARP onto ongoing anti-VEGF therapy in a high-VTE patient.

expected_benefit: SOLO1 PFS HR 0.30 (0.23-0.41), mPFS 56.0 vs 13.8 mo, with a mature 7-year OS benefit HR 0.55 (0.40-0.76), p=0.0004 - the highest-quality replicated long-term survival readout in the dossier. The mechanistic floor is solid (Bryant synthetic-lethality work; a BRCA2-mutant ovarian PDX).
key_risks: grade 3+ anemia 22% and an AML signal of 1.2% over long follow-up, both relevant to her marrow-toxicity veto
strictly gated on a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation; her germline is wild-type, so this could be a dead end if the somatic call is negative
preference_alignment: Oral, matches 'oral preferred'. Anemia and the long-term myeloid risk press against her severe-myelosuppression veto, but the single-agent profile is cleaner than the olaparib + bevacizumab stack on the bleeding axis.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 category 1, but only for BRCA-mutated tumors; her germline is wild-type and the somatic call is pending, so she is currently outside that population.
rationale_summary: Conditional on a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation. This is the highest-quality evidence in the set - the lowest RoB, the largest effect, and the only mature OS readout - but eligibility is the narrowest, since SOLO1 enrolled only BRCA-mutated tumors and her germline is wild-type. Risktaker (rank 4, the reserve play that activates the moment a somatic variant returns), critic (rank 2 on RoB), and concensusite (rank 4 on the conditional guideline gate) all endorse it but keep it below the broader options precisely because its gate is narrower than the HRD-score gate that opens olaparib + bevacizumab. No persona dissented or vetoed. Foreclosed if the somatic BRCA call is wild-type.
open_questions: Whether the tumor NGS returns a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation - the strict eligibility gate
Long-term myeloid risk (1.2% AML) over a multi-year maintenance window in a 70-79 patient
scenario_label: If a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation is confirmed on tumor NGS
likelihood_of_effect: High if somatic-BRCA-mutated (SOLO1 PFS HR 0.30, mPFS 56 vs 13.8 mo; 7-yr OS HR 0.55). Foreclosed if the somatic call is wild-type.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (anemia 22%, neutropenia 8%, AE discontinuation 11.5%; long-term AML 1.2%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cumulative myelosuppression and the long-term myeloid (AML) risk press on her marrow veto across a multi-year maintenance window

overall: Highest-quality evidence and the only mature OS readout, but the strictest gate - reachable only if tumor NGS returns a somatic BRCA1/2 mutation.

expected_benefit: A single non-randomized cohort in ER-positive high-grade serous disease: 60% vs 38.5% recurrence-free at 24 months (p=0.035). Preclinically the effect tracks ERalpha expression and runs partly through reduced tumor VEGF / microvessel density (Hirakawa 2014).
key_risks: evidence base is a tier-4 non-randomized cohort (ROBINS-I:Serious, n=80); no RCT-grade maintenance efficacy
PR-negativity and the weak-to-moderate ER intensity temper the expected magnitude
preference_alignment: Clears her whole preference set without conflict: oral once daily, no myelosuppression, no neuropathy, none of the bleeding/VTE risk. The cleanest match to her age and her stated preference for low-burden oral therapy.
guideline_status: NCCN Ovarian v3.2025 lists aromatase inhibitors among hormone-therapy options for ER-positive disease, but never elevates them to frontline maintenance alongside the category 1/2A PARP and bevacizumab data.
rationale_summary: Targets her ER-positive biology with the lowest toxicity of any option, which is why the advocate ranks it second and the conservative and concensusite both carry it as a low-burden holding option. The risktaker dissents that spending a high slot on a tier-4 endocrine signal inverts her efficacy-leaning 0.7 trade-off, and the critic asks (qualified, not dissent) that the ROBINS-I:Serious label and non-randomized design stay visible so the 60% figure is not read as RCT-grade. PR-negativity tempers the magnitude further. This reads as a low-toxicity maintenance or later-line holding strategy rather than a frontline backbone.
open_questions: Whether the endocrine signal holds in a PR-negative tumor with weak-to-moderate ER intensity
Sequencing relative to PARP / bevacizumab maintenance once the HRD score returns
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate (60% vs 38.5% recurrence-free at 24 mo, single non-randomized cohort, pmid:29157627); PR-negativity tempers it further.
toxicity_burden: Low (class effects: hot flushes, arthralgia, fatigue; no marrow or neuropathic toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: Cytostatic / antiangiogenic rather than cytotoxic; magnitude tempered by PR-negativity, so the holding effect may be shallow

overall: The one option that clears every preference axis, but on tier-4 evidence in a PR-negative tumor - a low-toxicity holding strategy, not a frontline backbone.

intervention_label: GEN-1 (IMNN-001) program incl. OVATION-3 maintenance trial
expected_benefit: OVATION-2 topline: median OS 40.5 vs 29.4 mo (HR 0.74); the BRCAm/HRD subgroup OS HR was 0.42 but on n=34 with a CI of 0.11-1.70 that crosses 1. OVATION-3 (NCT06915025) would let her layer PARP maintenance onto the IL-12 axis she is already on.
key_risks: efficacy rests on conference toplines (SITC 2024 / ASCO 2025) with no peer-reviewed primary paper, no PMID, and no structured safety table
intraperitoneal weekly dosing is higher-burden than her oral preference
preference_alignment: Honors prefers_trials and her existing on-study enrollment; no reported marrow or neuropathy signal that trips her vetoes. But intraperitoneal weekly dosing is higher-burden than her stated oral / low-infusion preference.
guideline_status: Investigational; no consensus guideline lists IL-12 immunogene therapy in this setting.
rationale_summary: Not recommended on the recommendation list, kept visible so the reader sees what was considered and why it was excluded. This targets her on-study IL-12 / tumor-microenvironment feature, so it is in scope as a feature-targeting intervention, but the critic vetoed it on evidence quality: ranking GEN-1 puts an unpublished result onto a treatment list, with the BRCAm/HRD subgroup resting on n=34 and an OS HR CI of 0.11-1.70 that crosses 1. That veto rests on the published-evidence base, not on the biomarker, so it does not lift with HRD confirmation. The concensusite dissents on guideline fit (no consensus guideline lists it; it belongs in her on-study context). The risktaker and advocate carry it as a trial-continuity option for a trial-preferring patient already responding on the regimen. It stays a not_recommended row: the on-study program is her treating team's and the trial's conversation, not a Libby recommendation.
open_questions: Whether a peer-reviewed OVATION-2 primary publication with a structured safety table changes the evidence read
Whether OVATION-3's PARP-maintenance arm applies to her, which itself depends on the pending HRD / somatic-BRCA result
likelihood_of_effect: Unestablished. OVATION-2 topline OS HR 0.74 with no peer-reviewed primary paper; the BRCAm/HRD subgroup CI (0.11-1.70) crosses 1 on n=34.
toxicity_burden: Low (intraperitoneal IL-12 manageable in prior GEN-1 work; no structured per-term safety table public; no marrow or neuropathy signal)

counter_productive_moa.description: The critic veto stands on evidence-quality grounds: an unpublished result with a subgroup CI crossing 1 cannot anchor a treatment recommendation

overall: Considered and not recommended: targets her on-study IL-12 axis but rests on unpublished conference toplines the critic vetoed - the on-study program is the trial's and treating team's conversation.
